runners_data.name: Ellie's de Vega
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner, has placed twice at 5f on Standard going with two runner-up finishes on turf; Philip Kirby yard is in fair form at 2/9 over 14 days, and with blinkers fitted she should break sharply and set a manageable pace — the key question is whether she can sustain it over the final furlong having done all the work.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Ellie's de Vega nonetheless boasts a second two starts back and another second three starts back, underlining his consistency at this level; drawn in stall nine carrying 128 lb, the concern is that sixth last time out clouds his recent momentum.

runners_data.name: Shatin Venture
runners_data.note: Excellent Standard-going record (14 runs, 1 win, 6 places) and five of her last five runs all over this course and distance; though her natural style is hold-up and the midfield map position does not reflect her true role, her deep course familiarity and fitness after 180 days off is the more pressing factor to weigh here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Shatin Venture returns after a 180-day absence, which is the sharpest concern here; a second three starts back offers a crumb of comfort, but he faces a stiff task from stall 4 off a mark of 46.

runners_data.name: Muddy Nora
runners_data.note: Three-year-old whose best form has come on Good ground over 6f rather than this quicker AW surface at 5f; naturally a hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map but unlikely to get a true stalking position given the field composition, and the drop to 5f on Standard may stretch her further.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Muddy Nora faces a stiff task, though a third two starts back offers a rare glimmer and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Let's Go Hugo
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 5f wins on Standard at this track is the standout form line in the race; fitted with a hood and ridden by a 5lb claimer, he has a hold-up style on paper but his recent wins suggest he travels prominently — he is the primary danger to the leader regardless of how the scenario unfolds.
runners_data.comment: Let's Go Hugo arrives in red-hot form, winning back-to-back last time out and two starts back, and he handles today's trip and conditions having tackled both before; the main risk is whether 140 lb blunts his momentum.

runners_data.name: Papa Don't Preach
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with solid Standard-going form (9 runs, 1 win, 4 places) and confirmed prominent running style — the only runner who might genuinely challenge Ellie's de Vega for the early lead; has course-and-distance placed form and is the biggest tactical threat to the favourite shape.
runners_data.comment: Placed efforts two and three starts back give Papa Don't Preach solid recent claims, and he has run over today's trip and going before; fit enough at 16 days since his last start, the 135 lb burden is the main query, though our rating of 66 suggests he holds serious untapped potential.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Terms
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with two placed efforts on Standard ground; trainer Iain Jardine in strong 14-day form (3/21), and a second to a rival on this surface last time out suggests ability, but the crowded hold-up division makes a clear passage from the rear problematic.
runners_data.comment: Pivotal Terms carries 132 lb from stall eight yet our rating of 66 marks her out as the one to beat in this field, having run over today's trip and going before; the concern is she has been winless in her last six starts, with a best of second four starts back.

runners_data.name: Heathers Feather
runners_data.note: Best form has come at longer trips (7f-10f on turf and AW) rather than at the minimum 5f here; hold-up style mapped to its natural position, but both the trip and the surface represent untested territory based on recent history — hood fitted but unconvincing profile for this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than fourth in recent starts, Heathers Feather is hard to fancy on our ratings from stall one, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick turnaround of just 14 days.

runners_data.name: Sands Of Seve
runners_data.note: Has placed twice in 14 runs on Standard ground and showed a bold second at 5f on Good recently; naturally a hold-up horse whose style fit score of 0.91 flags a likely compromise of position in this hold-up-heavy field — form is creditable but the tactical situation works against him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sands Of Seve has at least run over today's trip and going before, and a second four starts back offers some encouragement, though consecutive sixth-place efforts two and three starts back are harder to ignore at a mark of 52.

runners_data.name: Lady Bouquet
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on Good ground last time, giving her a live each-way profile, but has yet to win on Standard; another genuine hold-up type pushed into the midfield map picture — her style fit of 0.94 is the best of the redistributed group, yet the pace shape still makes her a late-finishing challenge against a front-runner likely to dictate.
runners_data.comment: Won on her most recent start and arrives here just nine days later with experience of today's trip and conditions in her favour, though that ninth two runs back is a concern and she carries 130 lb from stall seven.

races.paceDynamic: Ellie's de Vega is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Newcastle AW sprint and looks set to enjoy an uncontested lead from the outset, able to dictate her own rhythm without pressure from a genuine challenger. The remainder of the field is heavily populated with hold-up types — Shatin Venture, Muddy Nora, Sands Of Seve and Lady Bouquet are all natural hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield map position because true rear-runners are over-represented in this line-up; Papa Don't Preach is the only realistic prominent challenger but is unlikely to overpower the leader into a frantic pace. With Standard going on Newcastle's flat 5f track, a controlled early gallop from Ellie's de Vega creates a race that is genuinely leader-friendly — those trying to close from behind must overcome the dual disadvantage of a slow-burn early pace and limited ground to make it up. This shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can race prominently or track the leader in the first two, with Let's Go Hugo and Papa Don't Preach best placed to exploit early positions while true closers face a stern test getting to the front in time. The field holds more hold-up types than can secure their natural position, with Papa Don't Preach and Let's Go Hugo most likely to actually press forward and fill the prominent slots behind Ellie's de Vega.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ellie Leads Untouched
scenarios.trigger: If Ellie's de Vega breaks cleanly and controls a comfortable solo lead without Papa Don't Preach applying pressure.
scenarios.body: Ellie's de Vega dictates a measured gallop on the flat Newcastle 5f, conserving energy through the early sectionals and stretching clear when she picks up in the final furlong; Standard going suits her confirmed form at the course and distance. Horses tracking prominently in second and third — Let's Go Hugo and Papa Don't Preach — are best placed to chase her down, but with no rivals applying pressure early, she may prove very hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Papa Don't Preach challenges Ellie's de Vega from an early stage and the race becomes a genuine two-horse contest for the lead.
scenarios.body: A contested pace lifts the tempo and begins to play into the hands of those tracking just off the lead, with Let's Go Hugo ideally positioned in third to pounce if the two leaders tie each other up late. Papa Don't Preach's course-and-distance form on Standard ground gives it the credentials to match strides with the leader and potentially overhaul her in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Cuts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and drains the leaders, allowing a well-timed hold-up run to land the spoils.
scenarios.body: Shatin Venture has the best same-going profile in this field with 14 runs on Standard and a record of placing prominently, and though redistributed from its true hold-up style, its course familiarity and fitness edge over the layoff is a minor concern; Pivotal Terms has placed twice on Standard and brings straightforward credentials for a late challenge. Both benefit if the front two burn each other out, but the flat 5f Newcastle track and a likely moderate tempo make this the least reliable route to victory for genuine closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Ellie's de Vega misses the break or is crowded early and the race temporarily lacks a clear leader.
scenarios.body: A scrambled early order on 5f at Newcastle with no dominant pace figure would create a bunched, messy contest where any horse with a clear run at the furlong pole could strike; Let's Go Hugo's recent back-to-back 5f wins on Standard and his headgear suggest he handles messy races competitively. This scenario is low-probability given Ellie's de Vega's confirmed front-running style and the straightforward Newcastle layout.

watchPoints.text: Ellie's de Vega's gate break is the pivotal moment — if she misses the kick or is crowded in stall, the entire race shape collapses and the scenario probabilities restructure dramatically.

Let's Go Hugo carried a big weight (140lbs) to back-to-back wins at this track and trip; watch whether Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) can handle that burden tactically without losing position in the early stages.

Papa Don't Preach is the only horse likely to press Ellie's de Vega for the lead — watch the first furlong to see whether he commits forward, as that determines whether this is a solo-led race or a contested one.

The hold-up contingent (Shatin Venture, Muddy Nora, Sands Of Seve, Lady Bouquet) is so numerous that at least one will be shuffled wider or further back than intended at the break — watch for traffic issues turning into the final 2f on the straight Newcastle track.
Shatin Venture returns from 180 days off; watch market moves close to post time for any significant support that would suggest connections are confident about fitness despite the layoff.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Blairtum Night
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse in a field that pushes it into midfield; Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim is a small positive but the horse has shown no wins or places on Standard AW going across four efforts, making it difficult to get enthusiastic here despite the competitive OR of 50.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Blairtum Night at least returns fit on 14 days' rest and has run over today's trip and going, though a career-best effort is needed from stall one carrying 131 lb off an official mark of 50.

runners_data.name: Sassy Glory
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — won over this exact course, distance and Standard going last time out and clearly relishes the flat Newcastle mile; Mark Walford has no runners in the past 14 days but the 25-day break appears managed, and the visor has been a key headgear trigger in the horse's best form.
runners_data.comment: Sassy Glory returns 25 days after a win three starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going gives her every chance under 130 lb from stall 10; the risk is that her two most recent efforts have disappointed.

runners_data.name: Elettaria
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer by inclination but forced into a midfield slot here given the glut of closers; the seven-year-old has a solid placing record on Good ground and Cam Hardie is a positive booking, though the switch to Standard AW going — with only one win or place in six tries on similar surfaces — gives pause.
runners_data.comment: Elettaria returns after 21 days carrying 128 lb from stall 9, and her second last time out offers a clear positive, though she remains winless in her last six starts and that patchy overall sequence — including a fifth two starts back — suggests she finds winning elusive.

runners_data.name: One More Bottle
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh partners a horse that wants to come from off the pace but will find itself in the middle of the pack throughout; the form string includes a zero placing record on Standard AW going across three attempts, and the blinkers have not unlocked improvement, so the style mismatch compounds an already modest profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, One More Bottle at least returns on a handy 25-day break with experience over today's trip and conditions, though his recent finishes make it hard to fancy him reversing the slide from stall four.

runners_data.name: Soda
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides a three-year-old carrying 126lbs; the horse has only one placing on Standard AW going in six tries and the modest recent form (including a ninth on Good ground) doesn't encourage, though its natural hold-up style is at least honest in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Soda faces a stiff ask here, though third last time out offers a sliver of encouragement and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Furrst Lady
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a significant concern in a race where hold-up types are pushed forward and asked to travel prominently; Roger Fell's two runners in the past 14 days shows stable activity, but nine runs without a win or place on Good or Standard across the last five is damning, and the style displacement makes this harder still.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with finishes no better than seventh in recent outings, Furrst Lady is hard to fancy on these figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 21 days since her last outing leaves her reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Queenies Pal
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby has two winners from nine runners in the past fortnight suggesting a stable in reasonable form; the 48-day absence is the key flag here, and the tongue-tie plus cheekpieces combination hasn't produced a win from nine career starts — the 3yo is pushed into midfield against its instincts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Queenies Pal is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's trip and going before and draws stall two carrying 121 lb.

runners_data.name: Book Of Life
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides a horse with a deeply consistent placing record — six places from 13 runs on Standard going — making it one of the most reliable profiles in the race for surfaces and trip; the 7-day turnaround is brisk but the horse clearly handles quick returns, and a prominent or mid-division run suits the shape if it can track Sassy Glory.
runners_data.comment: Book Of Life has shown real consistency in recent starts, finishing third last time out and a second three starts back, and he handles today's distance and going, all of which underpin his strong standing in the ratings; the risk is that he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Mercurius Power
runners_data.note: The only genuine prominent-style runner outside the leader; Jack Dace's 5lb claim helps offset the top weight feel, and the horse has five places from 13 Standard going runs showing real course affinity — the headgear (tongue-tie, cheekpieces) is established, and tracking Sassy Glory from second is a clean tactical position in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Mercurius Power has run over today's trip and going, and his latest second suggests a return to form after a mid-sequence dip, with draw three and a rating of 61 offering encouragement; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Hear The Drums
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim on a three-year-old rated 55 with two career wins on Standard going is interesting; the fade flag is a concern and the horse's best form came at shorter or on Soft ground, but if the gallop is compressed it retains enough ability to feature — the 27-day break looks routine for the Fahey yard.
runners_data.comment: Hear The Drums bounced back to winning form last time out and, with experience of today's trip and going, conditions look to suit; the 27-day break should leave him fresh, and 131 lb is workable for a gelding who has shown he can win at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Sassy Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner in this ten-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her, she should be able to dictate a sustainable, measured gallop from the gates on this flat Newcastle AW mile. Mercurius Power is the only true prominent-style runner and will likely slot in directly behind her, giving the race a two-horse vanguard setting a controlled tempo rather than a scorching pace. At standard going on a flat track with a lone pace-setter setting her own fractions, this shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can travel into the race without burning energy — the race is likely to be won from the front two or three throughout. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Blairtum Night, Elettaria, One More Bottle, Furrst Lady and Queenies Pal are all genuine hold-up horses who will be forced forward into midfield positions, but of those, none is likely to truly secure a natural front position — Sassy Glory and Mercurius Power are best placed to control the shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sassy Glory Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Sassy Glory leads uncontested at a steady-to-fair gallop and Mercurius Power travels prominently in her slipstream.
scenarios.body: Sassy Glory sets her own pace on the flat track and, with no rival willing or able to pressure her early, conserves energy to extend into the straight; this shape rewards the horse who has dictated and the prominent tracker directly behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Mercurius Power or Book Of Life tracks the leader closely and has enough in reserve to overhaul Sassy Glory in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A controlled front-running tempo suits a prominent horse who has been travelling sweetly and can quicken past a tiring leader late; Book Of Life's consistent placing record at this trip on Standard ground gives it a strong profile in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and midfield runners such as Elettaria or Hear The Drums find a clean passage to accelerate past a field that has bunched up.
scenarios.body: A very slow early tempo can compress the field and allow a horse from the mid-division with a late turn of foot to pick off tiring rivals; Hear The Drums has won at this trip on Standard going and retains ability if fitness is there, while Elettaria places consistently on similar ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Held-Up Closer Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough to string the field out and allow a true hold-up horse to pick up pieces late in the straight.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Sassy Glory to go hard early — unlikely given no pace rival — making it the least probable shape; any of the redistributed hold-up types could theoretically benefit but their forced midfield positions mean they are racing out of role throughout.

watchPoints.text: Sassy Glory controls the tempo entirely alone — if she quickens at any point before the two-furlong pole, the field that has been pushed forward into unfamiliar midfield positions may not respond quickly enough to bridge the gap.

Mercurius Power's tactical position directly behind the leader is the race's key secondary move — watch whether Jack Dace elects to sit on Sassy Glory's heels from the start or gives her daylight, as that decision shapes whether the leader is pressured at all.

Several hold-up horses — particularly Furrst Lady and Queenies Pal — carry fade flags and are being asked to race out of their natural role in midfield; if they are pushed forward early, they may tire badly in the final two furlongs and cause interference as the field narrows.

Book Of Life's seven-day turnaround and consistent Standard going form makes it the most interesting dark-horse profile — watch whether Jason Hart elects to track the pace prominently or drops in, as the horse's record suggests it is at its best when racing off a strong gallop rather than a dawdle.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Soham's Roger
runners_data.note: Long-absent (310 days off) and dropped in class to OR 49, racing off an unfashionable yard with no recent form to lean on; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is at the back of the field, so the mile's controlled tempo offers little help in generating the late acceleration he needs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning after a 310-day absence, Soham's Roger is a difficult proposition ranked last on our figures, with a speed rating of 44 underlining the concern; he has run over today's trip before, but that counts for little given the overall profile.

runners_data.name: Here Comes Louie
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's three-year-old has placed twice on Standard AW going at this trip (2/8f/STA, 2/8f/STA) and carries only 129lbs for a 5lb claimer; a hold-up operator by style, though one who has shown he can race closer when needed, and the proximity of his last run (25 days) is a positive.
runners_data.comment: Here Comes Louie has finished second in two of his last five starts and returns here on fitting distance and going experience, carrying 129 lb from stall two, with our rating of 58 giving him strong claims — though he remains yet to win and that seventh last time out is the concern.

runners_data.name: Itszaboy
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler runner with a persistent form string of near-misses and mid-division finishes on Good ground who has yet to show he can reproduce that form on AW Standard; his natural style is to sit and wait, and with the race map already crowded at the rear, getting the position he needs will be genuinely difficult in this field shape.
runners_data.comment: Itszaboy has run over today's trip and steps back out after 25 days, bringing a second last time out as his chief credential, though he remains winless in his last five starts and a speed rating of 47 hints he may need improvement to land this.

runners_data.name: Walk On Walk On
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's three-year-old carries headgear and has two placed efforts at this trip on Good going, suggesting he stays the mile comfortably; a hold-up type who has found a way to place in competitive races, and the trainer's 2/9 14-day record shows form is live right now.
runners_data.comment: Ran second two starts back and returns here 36 days on from his latest outing, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; winless in recent starts but our figures see enough here to make him of clear interest from stall four carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Lady Delila
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris mare with excellent Standard AW experience (9 runs on that surface), placing three times including at this trip, and headgear retained; naturally races from off the pace and has the course-and-going profile to be competitive, though a lone front-runner setting a controlled tempo is not the catalyst she needs to really shine.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Lady Delila heads here ranked bottom two on our figures, and an eighth last time out does little to inspire confidence; 58 days off the track adds another question mark, though she has run over today's trip and going before and carries a workable 127 lb.

runners_data.name: The Floors Munky
runners_data.note: Gary Rutherford's three-year-old has a worrying pattern of finishing last or near-last, including three consecutive zeros in recent form, and the ⚠ fade flag underlines a tendency to stop in the home straight; bumped up to a mile having largely raced over sprint trips, with Standard AW form that offers no encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, The Floors Munky nonetheless rates above his official rating on our figures, suggesting he is better than his handicap rating implies, and he has run over today's trip and going; the risk is a string of unplaced efforts that demand a significant turnaround in form.

runners_data.name: Barleybrown
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's six-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner in the race and carries 135lbs for Joanna Mason, who knows this track well; placed twice on Standard AW going at this trip, and with no rival likely to dispute the lead, she is in a career-best tactical position even if her overall form profile is modest.
runners_data.comment: Barleybrown shaped with promise when second three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating marking him out as the one to beat in this field; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from two disappointing efforts since.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt runner who won at this trip on Standard AW (1/8f/STA) but that win came some time ago and AW form since has been ordinary; races from hold-up position naturally and, with the field packed with closers, getting a clear run in the straight on a day when the pace may not collapse is a genuine concern.
runners_data.comment: Defence Missile won two starts back but has otherwise struggled, finishing outside the top five in three of his last five starts, and our figures rank him seventh of nine here. Has run over today's trip and returns after 32 days off, but he is hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Thunder Rush
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood's lightly raced three-year-old has just three starts, all on Standard AW including this trip, with a best finish of fifth; form string of 570 gives little to work with, and a 41-day break with no trainer 14-day runners in form means he arrives with plenty of unknowns.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked sixth of nine on our ratings, Thunder Rush does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, though his recent sequence of unplaced efforts offers little encouragement despite a feasible weight of 132 lb from stall one.

races.paceDynamic: Barleybrown is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no rival likely to press hard for the lead from the outset, she should be able to bowl along at a controlled, honest but not brutal gallop on Standard ground over the mile. With no genuine pace duel to sap her reserves, she will dictate terms from the front, set a rhythm that suits her, and force those behind to make their moves earlier than ideal. The redistribution note is important here: Soham's Roger, Itszaboy, Lady Delila, The Floors Munky and Defence Missile are all true hold-up horses mapped forward on the visual because the field is saturated with closers — in reality, most will settle towards the rear and face a straightforward single-pace gallop that gives them little sectional change to exploit late. This shape firmly favours a front-runner or a horse able to race prominently just off Barleybrown, saving ground and kicking into the straight, rather than a pure late finisher waiting for a pace collapse that is unlikely to materialise at this controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Barleybrown Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Barleybrown goes clear from the gate and no rival has the early pace or inclination to close the gap before halfway.
scenarios.body: Barleybrown settles into a comfortable lead, dictates a fair but steady gallop, and the field behind never applies meaningful pressure until it is too late to claw back the advantage entering the straight. Any horse able to race in second or third without expending excess energy is the main beneficiary, and Barleybrown herself is in her optimal scenario having secured an uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough that a horse tracking Barleybrown two to three lengths off the pace can peel away in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Here Comes Louie, who has twice placed at this course and distance on Standard going, is ideally set up to sit just off the pace and sprint past a tiring Barleybrown inside the final furlong; Walk On Walk On, placed here on Good ground, is a credible second option from just off the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough — perhaps Barleybrown is pushed wider or quickens too soon — to open ground for hold-up horses coming from mid-to-rear in the straight.
scenarios.body: Lady Delila has solid AW form on Standard going with three placed efforts in similar company and could thread through if the leaders tie up; Defence Missile won on Standard ground at this trip and is capable of a late run if the fractions are genuinely demanding. Both face the challenge of a likely single-pace gallop that historically does not generate the sectional collapse closers need.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Finish, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Barleybrown either stumbles at the start or is harried into going too fast and stops, causing a concertina effect with no clear winner emerging from the pack.
scenarios.body: In a genuinely compressed finish where tactical positioning matters, horses drawn or positioned centrally with a clear run could benefit from gaps opening late; Thunder Rush and Soham's Roger, though lightly raced at this track, could steal a placing if chaos reigns. This is the least likely shape given the clearly defined pace picture.

watchPoints.text: Barleybrown goes unchallenged to the front — if Joanna Mason gets an uncontested lead inside the first furlong, the race is effectively set in stone from that point and all hold-up horses are immediately compromised.

Here Comes Louie's positioning in the first half-mile is critical — if Conor Whiteley (5lb claim) can slot into second or third without fighting for it, he has the course-and-going profile to be dangerous in the straight.

Walk On Walk On wears headgear and has a history of prominent-to-midfield finishes; if Philip Kirby's runner travels sweetly in the first half, the standard AW pace scenario suits a horse that can quicken off a steady tempo.

The cluster of true hold-up horses — Soham's Roger, Itszaboy, Lady Delila, The Floors Munky and Defence Missile — means the rear of the field will be crowded, and any of them losing their position or getting boxed in at the turn into the straight will almost certainly end their winning chance in a race with no predicted pace collapse.

Thunder Rush's inexperience (three career runs) and 41-day absence make him an unpredictable factor — watch for him in the betting market as a clue to whether connections have seen enough at home to suggest improvement.
